question: AUTHORIZE THE MERGE of PR #238, or send it back for one sentence? Review returned GO with no material finding, and the FO arbiter reproduced its four recorded findings. One needs your ruling because the text in question is your own amendment, transcribed verbatim, and this document is promoted into SECURITY.md unchanged. Doc line 46 says six of the ten harnesses have no event adapter and can never emit session_ended. That is literally true, but only Claude and Gemini can actually emit it — Codex has no SessionEnd mapping and Antigravity's hook sends only store_changed — so eight of ten rows can never be probed, not six. Two options: merge as-is and file the correction against DRC-4037, or authorize a one-sentence reword now and re-run a two-minute prose CI cycle before merging.

artifacts.summary:
Both lenses ran as separated passes and every measurement in the deliverable reproduced. The two git flags were cross-tested for independence in six throwaway repositories: each disarms exactly one hazard and neither disarms the other's, against a no-probe control. The changed count really is 2 entries for 4 files. All five code citations resolve to the exact lines claimed, and the document's SECURITY.md citation is right where DEC-3's own is off by one line. The document matches the amended bounds character-for-character on the nullable surface and names session_ended rather than the finished_at turn-stop stamp, with both non-reproducing figures absent — zero occurrences of twice, unconditional, or finished_at.

The escalation trigger was tested rather than waved off. Recovering the quota precedent from 7134a01 showed that every structure that might have counted as beyond the seven elements is the precedent's own shape — the section-local violation clause, the intro-amendment section down to the phrasing, and a flag-table bullet that is the line-for-line analogue of ours. That converted a plausible blocker into an evidenced pass.

AC2 was proven from the mechanism rather than from the report: the aggregator passes a skipped job only when the detector said code=false and refuses to report at all if the detector did not succeed, so quality-gate passing with all five skipped is itself the proof. All three runs were verified by API to carry head 9d9059f, so no superseded-head green. AC7 was reproduced at both ends, and the quota document's intro amendment is live in SECURITY.md today, which proves the promotion mechanism rather than just the promotion. Copilot left zero inline comments, zero top-level reviews and zero issue comments, and no review was ever requested, so nothing was merged past.

Four findings, none material, none fixed by the reviewer. The FO arbiter reproduced the one needing a ruling and confirms it: Codex has no SessionEnd in its event map and registers none in its hook manifest, Antigravity's hook emits only store_changed, and only two mappings in event_hook.py produce session_ended. A second finding vindicates the implementation: the amendment's own refutation of the twice figure is conditional on hook exit code — a failing hook runs the script exactly twice at git 2.55.0 across three trials, a well-behaved one runs once — and because the document carries no run count it is correct under both. A third confirms the race-resolution characterisation by measuring a genuinely settled repository writing nothing across four runs. The fourth notes the working-directory retention claim is the one DEC-3 flagged as only partly true, and belongs in DRC-4037's design rather than this PR.
